data.summary: A disposable proof-of-concept directory containing a single Dockerfile that bakes the mise toolchain manager into a sandbox base image at build time. It simulates a hypothetical mise-managed rust/opencode preset and is explicitly marked as not-for-merge, so it carries no production business logic or APIs.

file_insights.name: Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: PoC Dockerfile that installs the mise binary, then uses it to provision pinned Rust and opencode versions on top of sandbox-base. It is explicitly disposable and not intended for merge.
file_insights.source_summary: Declares FROM sandbox-base and three build args (MISE_VERSION=v2026.9.0, RUST_VERSION=1.93.1, OPENCODE_VERSION=1.18.24). A first RUN layer curl-installs the mise binary to a system path, and subsequent layers use mise to install the pinned Rust and opencode toolchain versions. No application code, services, or exported symbols are defined.
file_insights.detailed_description: This Dockerfile is a throwaway proof-of-concept (task #3, Phase B) validating mise as a build-time install engine inside a sandbox image. It layers the mise binary system-side and then uses mise to install pinned Rust and opencode versions, emulating a 'mise-managed rust/opencode preset' as described in the comments. Its comments state it is not for merge and lives only in mise-poc/, so it has no production role.
responsibilities: Bake the mise binary into the image system path
Install the pinned Rust toolchain via mise
Install the pinned opencode version via mise
Serve as a disposable validation artifact for the mise-based provisioning pattern
